page.layout: One column of verse, lines indented in varying amounts, centred on the page. Below the last line, a gathering mark at the foot, centred under the text.

main_text.p: Nobilibus meritum redonat. Nam quum supremi iussit ad ætheris Migrare sedes COELIPOTENS tuum FRATREM beatas, perque tempus Omne frui potiorus[?] aura Vitæ: & relictus quum tibi se lubens Summisit HERES IVNIOR, & tuis Cum gente dilecta regendos Consilius CASIMIRE fasces Subiecit: Isthæc clarior emicans Te cura cunctis impulit OPTIMI Præclara FRIDRICI PARENTIS Impauidum renouare[?] facta: Cuius revixit pectoribus fides Antiqua puris. Cui SAPIENTIÆ Consulta mens CÆLESTIS, atque Imperium fuit ampliare Propensa CHRISTI: cœtibus & pius Afferre præsens auxilium, simul Insanientum bella mouit PONTIFICVM furor inquietus. Qua laude vicit fata, & OLYMPICAS Emensus arces nunc fruitur DEO, Mensisque DIVORVM receptus

page.notes: The first line is the end of a stanza begun on the previous page. Printed words are set partly in small capitals and partly in italic; the capitalised words are copied in capitals as printed. "iussit" is copied as "iussit" (long s is plain s). "reuixit" is corrected to "revixit" because the v is a consonant. [?] on "potiorus" and "renouare": the letters are partly worn, so the readings are uncertain. The mark at the foot reads "* 3" or similar; it is a gathering signature, not a page number, and is uncertain. The top-left stanza has a lost or cut edge at the left margin; no text is missing from the printed lines as far as visible. The verse is one stanza, so it is one paragraph with printed line breaks kept.
